I'm pretty sure you mean your own personal death, but I read it as death in general so I am going to answer that way because it did change my outlook on just about everything. When I was sixteen, I found my dead mom in the laundry room. It ended up being a very complicated and confusing ordeal. I remember learning about Fractured Psyches where a traumatic event changes you a little, but this was like a complete obliteration and reformation of the psyche and I pretty much had to figure out how to think all over again. I'm very happy with who I am now though, so that's awesome.

I saw a woman die when when I was 14. She was dismounted from her horse when it was spooked during a ride through a forest. She wasn't wearing a helmet and suffered massive head and neck injuries. She died as paramedics arrived gurgling and choking in her own blood.

Fast forward 4 years and I started working in an A+E department and I am now working as a paramedic. I've seen countless people dead, and watched many of them die in front of my eyes, old and young alike.

It has changed me that's for sure. It has meant I have had to face my own mortality on a regular basis and realise the fragility of life and how quickly it can be taken from us. This has made me value my own life and those around me who I care for. I often find myself the most caring and loving with my kinfolk after caring for a patient who didn't make it that day.

I think not enough people think about death in our culture, when it comes it is such a shock to most because of this. By facing death in whatever form it takes can make you stronger and live life with energy, love and compassion.

When I was about 16, my friend and I were driving around, listening to music, smoking etc. We pulled up to an intersection. The light turned green. I said "Go." My friend just says "Wait." How did it change my outlook on life? I don't know. Don't really think about it.

I had a heart valve infection when I was 14. It was considered a flu by the emerg doctor until day five, when I started pissing blood, and just blood. Mind you before this I had many major warning sign symptoms, like jaundice from day 2, a constant fever of 103.5+, fever pains, inability to eat anything, couldn't breath deeply without triggering insanely painful coughing sessions, and so on.

We finally saw an emerg doc who did some blood work, got a prescription for meds, and sent me home warning my dad to keep a close eye on me. We got home after getting the meds and we had gotten a call telling us to come back 'right now'. My platelets were very low, which is to say I literally had next to no white blood cells.

We were at the hospital for about six hours, but it felt like 30 minutes to me because toxic shock was setting in. We then got transferred to the children's hospital, but they didn't send me in an ambulance. They made my dad drive. They later got bitched out by the doctor at the children's hospital. Words like lawsuit and medical malpractice were thrown around apparently.

By the time we got to the kid's hospital, I was literally 20 minutes from dead. I was very out of it. We got to registration and the nurse grabbed my arm to steady me, planning to get me to lay down on a gurney. She took a second look at me, brought me around a corner and hit what I thought looked like a huge red button bigger than her hand. It was red, but only about an inch in diameter.

I don't remember a lot after that, but I apparently flatlined over five times, and the nurses couldn't get any veins for IVs so they had to beat my arm black and blue and used the area as a pin cushion.

I finally stabilised, got moved to ICU, and stayed comatose for another five days.

I was on very powerful antibiotics for six weeks, hospitalized for only three though. Got out two days after christmas break started and had modified exams meaning I didn't have to catch up on the school work I missed.

I do still have a hole in my valve. And have to take antibiotics even just to get my teeth cleaned. Eventually I will need surgery, but for now my heart copes well with the hole and severe back leak into the first chamber.

Like many others, I'm an immigrant from reddit, and I'm happy to see this place is here. At reddit, I ended up unsubscribing from /r/luciddreaming because I found that the community there was a bit rigid for my tastes. The sidebar read:

Please take discussions of the paranormal such as out-of-body experiences, astral projection someplace else. Binaural beats are also inappropriate. Let's keep this in the realm of science.

Yes, there's science around it, and a few researchers finding some interesting observations, but it's hardly physics or chemistry (i.e. where the basic underlying phenomena are really well understood). I feel it's more in the realm of psychology or philosophy, where much is known, but much more is unknown. Others must have felt similarly, as /r/luciddreamingspec was created to fill the void for people whose explanations and experiences weren't generally popular. Its sidebar read:

A place for lucid dreaming discussion of topics that are not allowed in /r/LucidDreaming, paranormal, shared dreaming, etc.

For me, lucid dreaming is a crazy experience (that I've only really done twice), and I am not in any way turned off by how people want to speculate about how it works, or what their experiences might mean. For example, you might choose to interpret the information from your dream characters as your subconscious, or you might feel that they provide you with access to knowledge from outside of yourself. It does not matter to me. The important thing is that we have a place for these discussions.

If anyone vehemently disagrees, let's discuss. If there truly is a need for a /v/luciddreamingspec, that's fine too. I just feel that there's so much in common between the two, and that the shared experiences are far more important than the different interpretations.

Ditto -- I'm pretty interested in lucid dreaming and this was actually the first sub I tried to make yesterday when I signed up. I'm in the process of writing a free ebook on lucid dreaming, I'll be sure to link it here once I finish it.

I was feeling the same way. There were some interesting posts but it was more about first-timers and redirecting them to the 'sidebar' as well as people's dreams which were sometimes entertaining and sometimes just repetitive. If we have more of a mix, I bet that this'll be a really diverse subverse and everyone will enjoy it. It probably won't need to branch out is what I'm trying to say.
